title: Tens of Millions of Red Crabs Take Over an Island and Close Its Roads

scenes.text: Tens of millions of red crabs take over this island.
scenes.keywords: red crabs migration road christmas island

scenes.text: It's Christmas Island, in the Indian Ocean. When the first big rains arrive, the crabs head from forest to sea.
Roads close. Workers build barriers and bridges so the crabs can cross.
A single female can lay more than 100,000 eggs.
The migration can start as early as October and run as late as January, depending on the rain and the moon.
Tens of millions of crabs, one island, and the roads are theirs.

description:
Every year, tens of millions of red crabs on Australia's Christmas Island leave the forest and march to the sea to spawn, closing roads on the way.
Females can lay more than 100,000 eggs, and workers build barriers and bridges to help the crabs cross safely.
Would you drive through a crab migration?
thumbnail_text: MILLIONS OF CRABS CLOSE THE ROADS
first_comment: The crabs' timing depends on the first heavy rain of the wet season and the phases of the moon. Which animal migration would you travel to see?
